lines.text: # comprehende-143: Smaller diffs on mobile, plus an Iosevka toggle
PR #143. No ticket, one conversation comment. Two UI stories in one PR: diffs shrink and wrap on narrow screens, and a header toggle switches the mono font to a bundled Iosevka.
- Why: present or absent. The PR body gives the mobile problem (long lines cut off at the card edge) and no reason for the font toggle.
- Parts: two. The PR title says "plus"; the font toggle could have been its own PR. A third part is fine for the mobile file header when it sits apart.

1. Narrow-screen diffs: `src/ui/lib/narrow.ts`, `src/ui/lib/narrow.test.ts`, `src/ui/PierreDiff.tsx`, `src/ui/components/HunkView.tsx`, `src/ui/lib/gap-style.ts`, and the breakpoint rules in `src/ui/styles.css`. Smaller font and line height, default wrap, and a slimmer file header below 799px.

2. Iosevka toggle: `src/ui/lib/mono-font.ts`, `src/ui/lib/mono-font.test.ts`, `src/ui/lib/MonoFontProvider.tsx`, `src/ui/components/Header.tsx`, `src/ui/main.tsx`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`. The font choice, its store, the toggle, and the new `@fontsource/iosevka` dependency.
- Narrow screens wrap diff lines by default, and the user's wrap toggle still wins over that default.
- The mono font choice is stored in localStorage under `comprehende.mono-font`, with IBM Plex Mono as the default.
- The PR adds the `@fontsource/iosevka` dependency for the font toggle.
- The narrow-screen diff work and the font toggle are two parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- The diff font size and line height step down at the same 799px breakpoint as the body text.
- Do not put the font toggle in the same part as the narrow-screen diff changes.
- Do not add a `dependsOn` from the font toggle to the narrow-screen group.

- This case checks that a PR whose title joins two features with "plus" gets two parts. `App.tsx`, `MobileShell.tsx` and `styles.css` can hold hunks of both stories, so they have no `together` or `apart` expect.
# comprehende-145: Remove old .githooks leftovers and keep eval artifacts 7 days
PR #145. No ticket, no comments. Two unrelated changes in one PR: dead git-hook installer code is deleted, and the eval workflow keeps its run artifacts for 7 days.
- Why: present. The PR body gives a reason for each story: no pre-commit hook ran since the move to `.vite-hooks`, and eval artifacts filled the Actions storage quota.
- Size: trivial or small. One deleted script and its test, one deleted comment, and one workflow line.
- Parts: two. The PR body says "Separately"; either change could have been its own PR.
- Groups: 2. A third is fine when the `exec.ts` comment sits apart.
1. Old hook installer removal: `scripts/install-git-hooks.js`, `src/git/hooks.test.ts`, `src/git/exec.ts`. The deleted installer, the test that checked it, and the comment that pointed at it.
2. Eval artifact retention: `.github/workflows/eval.yml`. One added `retention-days: 7` line on the upload step.
- The `Upload eval run` step in `.github/workflows/eval.yml` now sets `retention-days: 7`, so eval artifacts expire after 7 days instead of the GitHub default.
- The PR deletes `scripts/install-git-hooks.js` and `src/git/hooks.test.ts`, and removes the `exec.ts` comment that said `GIT_DIR_VARS` is mirrored in that script.
- The hook removal and the retention change are two parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- The diff does not change how hooks are installed; the PR body says vite-plus `prepare` already sets `core.hooksPath`, and only clones with the old `.githooks` value need a one-time local fix.
- Do not put the workflow line and the hook removal in one group or one part.
- Do not add a `dependsOn` between the two groups.
- Do not say the PR changes hook installation code; it only deletes the old installer.
- This case checks that two unrelated changes become two parts. `parts` is exactly 2.
# vitadeck-127: Classify emoji above U+1F000 by Emoji_Presentation; gate tests/ with clang-format

PR #127, closes issue #119. Two comments. The issue asks for two small things, and the PR does each in its own commit: `clang-format.sh` now covers `tests/` with a one-time whitespace reformat of the harnesses, and the emoji classifier drops its `>= U+1F000` shortcut.
- Title: the PR title, or the issue title.
- Why: present. Issue #119 names both items as follow-ups from the review of #114.
- Parts: two. Issue #119 lists them as two separate items, and the PR body says the reformat commit is kept separate so it does not hide the real change.
- Groups: 2 to 4. The harness reformat is mechanical.
1. Emoji classification: `src/ui/glyph_cache.c`, `src/ui/glyph_cache.h`, and the new `expect_cluster` cases in `tests/glyph_cache_harness.c`.

2. Format gate on `tests/`: `scripts/clang-format.sh`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/vitadeck-build/SKILL.md`, and the whitespace-only reformat of the other harnesses, which can be a trailing mechanical group of the same part.
- `vd_emoji_cluster` no longer treats every codepoint at or above U+1F000 as emoji; it uses the Emoji_Presentation table, which now covers all of Unicode 17.
- A following skin tone now also starts an emoji cluster, so modifier sequences without U+FE0F still draw as one image.
- `scripts/clang-format.sh` `check` and `format` now cover `tests/`, and the other harness changes are whitespace only.
- The emoji fix and the format gate are two parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- The PR accepts that a non-emoji followed by a skin tone (`a🏻`) now draws only `a`.
- Do not put the harness reformat in the emoji part.
- Do not say the harness reformat changes test behavior.
- This case checks that one ticket with two independent items becomes two parts. `tests/glyph_cache_harness.c` holds hunks of both stories, so it has no expect.
# vitadeck-81: Report unhandled rejections, stop stb_ds seed race, log dropped events
PR #81, fixes issues #69 and #78. Two comments. Two independent runtime fixes, each with its own issue, plus a small log line for dropped input events.
- Why: present. Issue #69 asks to report unhandled promise rejections, and issue #78 reports a TSan race on `stbds_hash_seed`.
- Parts: two or three. The rejection tracker and the seed race fix each close their own issue. The dropped-event log can be a third part.
3. Dropped-event log: `src/core/event_queue.c`, `tests/event_queue_harness.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`. Can be its own part.

- `js_runtime.c` installs a QuickJS promise rejection tracker; a rejection that still has no handler after the microtask queue drains is reported as an uncaught error and shows the Deck App Failure Screen.
- The vendored `stb_ds.h` no longer advances the global `stbds_hash_seed` when it creates a hash map; it only reads it, and the hunk is marked `VitaDeck:`.
- `event_queue_push` now logs a warning when it drops an event on a full queue, and `CMakeLists.txt` links raylib into `event_queue_harness` for that `TraceLog` call.
- The rejection fix and the seed race fix are separate parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- `js_limits_harness` adds a case where a `catch` attaches in a later microtask, and that case must not fail the app.
- Do not put the `stb_ds.h` change in the same part as the rejection tracker.
- Do not add a `dependsOn` between the rejection and seed race groups.
- This case checks that two fixes that close two issues become two parts.
# vitadeck-99: Record vendored patches; upload_vita syncs emoji assets

PR #99, fixes issues #87 and #93. Three comments. Two independent chores, each closing its own issue: a record of local patches to vendored code, and an `upload_vita` step that uploads the emoji images.
- Why: present. Issue #87 asks to record vendored patches, and issue #93 reports missing emoji after a code-only upload.
2. Emoji upload: `CMakeLists.txt` and the `vitadeck-build` skill note.
- `vendor/PATCHES.md` lists each local change to vendored code: `stb_ds.h`, `jimp/jimp.h`, and the `quickjs` submodule.
- `upload_vita` now uploads the emoji PNGs through one curl config written at configure time, and a stamp per build directory and Vita IP skips the step when the images did not change.
- The patch record and the emoji upload are two parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- The `stb_ds.h` hunk restores upstream's trailing newline, so the diff against upstream holds only the marked change.
- Do not put the `CMakeLists.txt` emoji upload in the patch record part.
- Do not add a `dependsOn` between the two parts.
- This case checks that two chores that close two issues become two parts.

+# vitadeck-81: Report unhandled rejections, stop stb_ds seed race, log dropped events
+
+PR #81, fixes issues #69 and #78. Two comments. Two independent runtime fixes, each with its own issue, plus a small log line for dropped input events.
+
+## Story
+
+- Title: the PR title.
+- Why: present. Issue #69 asks to report unhandled promise rejections, and issue #78 reports a TSan race on `stbds_hash_seed`.
+- Size: small or medium.
+- Parts: two or three. The rejection tracker and the seed race fix each close their own issue. The dropped-event log can be a third part.
+- Groups: 2 to 4.
+
+## Groups
+
+1. Unhandled rejections: `src/core/js_runtime.c`, `src/jslib/error.c`, `src/jslib/jslib.h`, `tests/js_limits_harness.c`, `CONTEXT.md`.
+2. stb_ds seed race: `vendor/stb_ds.h`.
+3. Dropped-event log: `src/core/event_queue.c`, `tests/event_queue_harness.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`. Can be its own part.
+
+## Must
+
+- `js_runtime.c` installs a QuickJS promise rejection tracker; a rejection that still has no handler after the microtask queue drains is reported as an uncaught error and shows the Deck App Failure Screen.
+- The vendored `stb_ds.h` no longer advances the global `stbds_hash_seed` when it creates a hash map; it only reads it, and the hunk is marked `VitaDeck:`.
+- `event_queue_push` now logs a warning when it drops an event on a full queue, and `CMakeLists.txt` links raylib into `event_queue_harness` for that `TraceLog` call.
+- The rejection fix and the seed race fix are separate parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
+
+## Good
+
+- `js_limits_harness` adds a case where a `catch` attaches in a later microtask, and that case must not fail the app.
+
+## Must not
+
+- Do not put the `stb_ds.h` change in the same part as the rejection tracker.
+- Do not add a `dependsOn` between the rejection and seed race groups.
+
+## Notes
+
+- This case checks that two fixes that close two issues become two parts.

+# vitadeck-99: Record vendored patches; upload_vita syncs emoji assets
+
+PR #99, fixes issues #87 and #93. Three comments. Two independent chores, each closing its own issue: a record of local patches to vendored code, and an `upload_vita` step that uploads the emoji images.
+
+## Story
+
+- Title: the PR title.
+- Why: present. Issue #87 asks to record vendored patches, and issue #93 reports missing emoji after a code-only upload.
+- Size: small or medium.
+- Parts: two.
+- Groups: 2 to 4.
+
+## Groups
+
+1. Vendored patch record: `vendor/PATCHES.md`, `vendor/jimp/README.md`, `docs/adr/0003-native-package-manifest-module.md`, `vendor/stb_ds.h`.
+2. Emoji upload: `CMakeLists.txt` and the `vitadeck-build` skill note.
+
+## Must
+
+- `vendor/PATCHES.md` lists each local change to vendored code: `stb_ds.h`, `jimp/jimp.h`, and the `quickjs` submodule.
+- `upload_vita` now uploads the emoji PNGs through one curl config written at configure time, and a stamp per build directory and Vita IP skips the step when the images did not change.
+- The patch record and the emoji upload are two parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
+
+## Good
+
+- The `stb_ds.h` hunk restores upstream's trailing newline, so the diff against upstream holds only the marked change.
+
+## Must not
+
+- Do not put the `CMakeLists.txt` emoji upload in the patch record part.
+- Do not add a `dependsOn` between the two parts.
+
+## Notes
+
+- This case checks that two chores that close two issues become two parts.
